identity.name: Crash
identity.one_liner: An asymmetric, distorted case built by Cartier's London workshop in 1967, sold since only in small, irregular batches rather than continuous production.

provenance_events.description: The Cartier Crash is designed at Cartier London in 1967 — the asymmetric, melted case allegedly inspired by a Cartier London timepiece that was in a car fire. Production has been limited and irregular for fifty years, making the Crash one of the most-cited vintage Cartier watches.

narrative.story: Cartier's London workshop produced the Crash in 1967, giving it an asymmetric, folded case that broke entirely from the brand's rectangular and round vocabulary. One frequently repeated account, attributed to auction specialist Paul Boutros, traces the design to a Cartier London executive whose Baignoire Allongée watch melted in a car fire; Cartier has never put the Crash into continuous production, instead releasing it in small, irregular runs and occasional Cartier Privé limited editions, including a 67-piece platinum Crash Skeleton in 2015.
narrative.collector_notes: The Crash is not one stable reference — case material, dial layout, and movement have changed across the 1967 original and later runs (the 2015 Skeleton uses manual caliber 9618 MC in a 45mm platinum case, distinct from the vintage 18K gold, caliber 841 pieces), so treat any Crash listing as its own specific variant rather than assuming a shared spec or price level.
